name: Developer tools
one_line: The platforms and tools developers pay to write, store, review and ship code — now the front line of the AI coding boom.
sells: Code hosting, version control, CI/CD, issue tracking, artifact management and AI coding assistants, sold by subscription and usage
customers: Software developers and the companies that employ them, from solo builders to large enterprises
suppliers: Cloud computing to run the platforms, and the AI labs whose frontier models power coding assistants

revenue.metric: estimated global revenue for developer platforms and AI coding tools
revenue.note: No clean single figure: market sizings vary widely by definition. The Business Research Company puts the narrow 'software development tools' market at $8.8B for 2026, but that excludes much of the collaboration-suite and AI-coding revenue counted here — the six listed vendors alone report about $13B+ combined (Atlassian's figure spans its whole suite). Treat ~$16B as an order-of-magnitude estimate.

structure.why: Hundreds of specialized vendors; The Business Research Company's tally puts the top ten at only about 16% of revenue. Code hosting itself concentrates around GitHub, but the wider toolchain — IDEs, CI/CD, artifact management, security, and now AI code editors — is split among many players, with AI-native entrants like Cursor reshaping the field.
structure.hhi_note: Shares not comparable across the fragmented market; vendor revenues span different product scopes, so no HHI is computed.

econ: Network effects and ecosystem lock-in. A developer platform grows more useful as more code, contributors and integrations gather in one place, so developers congregate where everyone already is. That tips code hosting toward a single dominant venue and lets the winner sell adjacent tools — CI/CD, security, AI assistants — up the stack, even while the broader tools market stays fragmented.
rank_basis: annual revenue or revenue run-rate from company filings and press, fiscal years ending 2025–2026; scopes differ (Atlassian spans its whole suite; Cursor and GitHub are run-rates; JetBrains is private and undisclosed)

companies.name: Atlassian
companies.note: Revenue spans Atlassian's whole suite (Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Jira Service Management), not only developer tools; up 26% YoY. Listed here because its tools anchor many developers' workflows.

companies.name: Cursor (Anysphere)
companies.note: AI-native code editor; figure is an ARR run-rate (Bloomberg, May 2026), not audited revenue. Parent Anysphere was acquired by SpaceX in Aug 2026.

companies.name: GitHub
companies.note: Run-rate cited by Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella; GitHub is a Microsoft subsidiary and does not report standalone audited revenue. Copilot passed 20M users in 2025.

companies.name: GitLab
companies.note: The independent, publicly traded DevSecOps platform; crossed $1B in ARR in FY2026, up 26% YoY.

companies.name: JFrog
companies.note: Software supply-chain / artifact management, the layer that stores and secures build outputs; up 24% YoY.

companies.name: JetBrains
companies.note: Private, so revenue is not disclosed (widely reported around $400M+ in prior years). Ranked last among listed vendors on that basis; rank uncertain. Maker of the leading paid IDEs.

products_note: Flagship products as of Nov 2026, checked against each vendor's own site and 2025–2026 coverage. Revenue figures are from company filings and press releases for fiscal years ending 2025–2026; scopes are noted where a figure spans more than developer tools.
